video_title: Jason Sudeikis Opens Up on Why Ted Lasso Is So Personal

quotes.speaker: Jason Sudeikis
quotes.summary_phrase: Jason Sudeikis on the personal nature of creating Ted Lasso
quotes.excerpt: you give a damn about each part of it. So then you're putting yourself in it.

text_blocks.speaker: Jason Sudeikis
text_blocks.text: Being involved with something from soup to nuts, from beginning to end, from conception to editing, you give a damn about each part of it. So then you're putting yourself in it.

quotes.speaker: Jason Sudeikis
quotes.summary_phrase: How writing and acting in Ted Lasso became a therapeutic process
quotes.excerpt: it almost becomes therapeutic where you start to recognize the things that you were thinking quietly.
quotes.quote: Even though I've had the good fortune of working at SNL, you get to write, I started as a writer there, so that stuff's from me, or through me, however you want to put it. Then we start to get to act it, then it's a little bit more you. You're always throwing the ball, and once a point guard, always a point guard, I say. You're always trying to make people look good too. But then this had this point of view that I'd had for a while, and it felt more like, with all the shit going on in the world, it was bubbling more to the surface. It almost becomes therapeutic where you start to recognize the things that you were thinking quietly, they're saying out loud, so it gives you the strength to think, I'd like to say it out loud yourself, and you realize how much more similar we are than we are different.

quotes.speaker: Jason Sudeikis
quotes.summary_phrase: Sudeikis on the wish fulfillment of playing a coach
quotes.excerpt: it's the wish fulfillment of getting to play a coach that I'd never had specifically.
quotes.quote: It's the wish fulfillment of getting to play a coach that I'd never had specifically, but always wish I had, the dad I wish I could be, the brother I wish I could be, the teammate. It's this, that, and the other, and you try to put all that in there. So yeah, it is very, very personal. And I'm glad it happened later in my life because if it would have happened early in my life, I'd be an asshole. I would have been like, I can do anything, look at me now.

quotes.speaker: Jason Sudeikis
quotes.summary_phrase: The impact of the pandemic on the success of Ted Lasso
quotes.excerpt: anything that helped us get out of what we all were dealing with, that brought healing.
quotes.quote: Anything that helped us get out of what we all were dealing with, that brought, I think, that was connecting people to something and things, I think, was healing. I don't know if we've taken fully the lessons that we all probably learned there. We may have got Mr. Miyagi'd by it all, like the pandemic, and we won't realize it until two minutes before we all die, that we're like, oh fuck, that's what the pandemic was.

quotes.speaker: Jason Sudeikis
quotes.summary_phrase: How Ted Lasso changed the cultural conversation around work-life balance
quotes.excerpt: it's changed the whole generation of people that we look at as being like, goddamn it.
quotes.quote: It's changed the whole generation of people that we look at as being like, goddamn it, we could have done a four-day work week. The whole generation is like, yeah, this is what we're doing because this is what we grew up in during that couple of years, this is what we knew and this is all, yeah. Casual Friday, fuck that, I'm not coming in on Friday. I'm going to work from home on Friday, from my house. I'm going to out-cat you. You think I'm going to just be happy with wearing khakis? I'm going to be in my fucking underwear and a dress shirt.

quotes.speaker: Jason Sudeikis
quotes.summary_phrase: Sudeikis on trusting his creative instincts for the show
quotes.excerpt: do I like it? Do I like the way we went about making it? I want to be proud.
quotes.quote: I didn't think anybody was going to like it. I mean, I knew I liked it. That's all you can do. That's all I can do. Is, do I like it? Do I like the way we went about making it? I want to be proud of that, proud of what we make, proud of how we make it. That's all you have control over.

quotes.speaker: Jason Sudeikis
quotes.summary_phrase: Applying John Wooden's philosophy to creative control
quotes.excerpt: don't concern yourself over which things you have no control over.
quotes.quote: There was that John Wooden quote, 'Don't concern yourself over which things you have no control over.' I'm sure he's paraphrasing someone else, but I believe in that. That's the only way to do it, because people will find you, especially in this day and age. You don't need, if you got talent, skill, whatever it is, they're going to find you. They're going to find you even if you don't.

quotes.speaker: Jason Sudeikis
quotes.summary_phrase: The origin of Ted Lasso in early NBC commercials
quotes.excerpt: Ted Lasso was based on these commercials we did like in 2013, 2014.
quotes.quote: Ted Lasso was based on these commercials we did like in 2013, 2014. The first one 2013, it was for NBC because they had got the Premier League on NBC. I remember being at the US Open with my friend John, and we're watching the tennis, and I looked down the row, and I see looking at me is Tony Parker and Thierry Henry. I recognize them both, couple of Frenchies, and they got their berets on, they're smoking. And they look at me, and they gave me smiles and the nod. I was like, I'm pretty sure that Tony Parker and Thierry Henry just gave me the nod like they recognized me.

quotes.speaker: Jason Sudeikis
quotes.summary_phrase: The moment Sudeikis realized the show's potential
quotes.excerpt: we love Ted Lasso. It was just the commercial at that point. I couldn't believe it.
quotes.quote: In between matches we go up and they're like, 'We love Ted Lasso.' It was just the commercial at that point. I couldn't believe it, and I was like, well, okay, well, this has legs. And then the second one, and so then that was just the commercials. Then by the time we got into the show, yeah, we've had all sorts, but from every world.

quotes.speaker: Jason Sudeikis
quotes.summary_phrase: The support from sports figures like Jurgen Klopp and Stan Kroenke
quotes.excerpt: Jurgen Klopp was big on us early on, which was really amazing.
quotes.quote: Jurgen Klopp was big on us early on, which was really amazing. And then, but I've even had Stan Kroenke, the owners of these giant sports teams come up and be like, 'Thank you for showing the humanity of owners.' You know, he's empathizing with Rebecca. It's like, so, yeah, it's nuts. It's nuts.

quotes.speaker: Jason Sudeikis
quotes.summary_phrase: Sudeikis on the joy of being called 'Coach' by real coaches
quotes.excerpt: I got such a kick out of walking around just like, you know, got the posture.
quotes.quote: I have friends that coach, they coach in high school, coach basketball, and they would come out when I was working in Las Vegas, doing Second City out there, they would take me to like their camps because they all come out to Vegas and they'd walk around, like, do you want to go? I was like, yeah. And I got such a kick out of walking around just like, you know, got the posture, walking around with other coaches and everybody calling everybody coach. I was like, it felt like a little wish fulfillment. It was great. And now I get to do it, people call me coach, and I'll turn around, think, it depends where we are.

quotes.speaker: Jason Sudeikis
quotes.summary_phrase: The challenge of breaking into the international soccer scene
quotes.excerpt: it is such a gatekeeping community that I totally respect and honor.
quotes.quote: It is such a gatekeeping community that I totally respect and honor, and like we came from a place of love, but there were, the commercials helped. I remember this one British guy after we had done the second commercial, we were doing a thing for, I think for Steve Nash's foundation, like before the, like where we played, you know, Coach Lasso and Coach Beard, and coached his foundation, like his charity game. And a British guy came up and goes, 'I love those commercials, you know, I can't do a French accent better than a British one,' and like, 'You got everything wrong perfectly.'

quotes.speaker: Jason Sudeikis
quotes.summary_phrase: Sudeikis's approach to learning soccer culture for the show
quotes.excerpt: for the first three seasons, I was agnostic. I took kits from everyone, I wore hoodies by everyone.
quotes.quote: For the first three seasons, I was agnostic. I took kits from everyone, I wore hoodies by everyone. People were like, who's your club? I used Man City on FIFA, like where a lot of the ideas for football came from. I'd sit there during the pandemic, I was, you know, smoking weed and drinking micheladas, got real good in my michelada mix, and kept a little yellow pad and I bought Xboxes for everybody, and PlayStation, I think Xboxes for everybody, and we got the codes. This was before the show had even come out, and we gave it to all the dudes that played on the team so we could all connect over the things.

quotes.speaker: Jason Sudeikis
quotes.summary_phrase: Sudeikis on the importance of mentorship in show business
quotes.excerpt: that's the thing that I try to encourage young folks coming up, you know, coming through SNL.
quotes.quote: That's the thing that I try to encourage young folks coming up, you know, coming through SNL, like that's a lot of people's first time in show biz. It was in many ways, it was certainly mine. I had access to it because a relative was in show business, but we never talked about business. We talked about the show part, you know, not the business part. But like, your reps work for you, like you forget they get a percentage of what you get, but how much of that, so then it's how important it is to find people that you know, or that you care about you, or that see you, see you completely.

quotes.speaker: Jason Sudeikis
quotes.summary_phrase: The power of saying 'no' in professional relationships
quotes.excerpt: especially if you're willing to say no. And the power of no is a very, very powerful thing.
quotes.quote: Especially if you're willing to say no. And the power of no is a very, very powerful thing. You know, it's a full complete sentence, and it's a powerful one too when used at the right time. And so yeah, we we've tried to handle that, you know, as well as you can without getting numbers like you used to do with Nielsen ratings and all that, and but yeah.

quotes.speaker: Jason Sudeikis
quotes.summary_phrase: The rapid development of Ted Lasso seasons two and three
quotes.excerpt: I remember we had started the writers room for season two early, like Apple greenlit that.
quotes.quote: I remember we had started the writers room for season two early, like Apple greenlit that. The show dropped on a Friday, like in August 2020, and on Monday, they called and were like, 'Hey, we want to pick you all up for a season two.' And then two weeks after that, 'Hey, can you add couple episodes to season two?' I know it's only 10 episodes, would you be willing to do 12? Two weeks after that, they're like, 'Would you, we want to give you a season three too.'
